title: Is the Tree a Mirror of Itself?

concept.title: Compare the left subtree with the mirror image of the right one
body: A tree is **symmetric** if its left half is the mirror image of its right half. Define the helper "are these two trees mirror images of each other?": two empty trees are mirrors; if only one is empty they are not; otherwise the roots must have equal values, the **left of the first** must mirror the **right of the second**, and the **right of the first** must mirror the **left of the second**.
This is the "same tree" check with the children **crossed**. A tree with only a root is symmetric; a root with exactly one child is not.

statement: A binary tree is symmetric if its left subtree is the mirror image of its right subtree (the same shape with left and right swapped, and the same values at the matching places). Decide whether the given tree is symmetric.
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
constraints: The height of a tree is at most 800.

examples.note: The left half (2 with 3, 4) mirrors the right half (2 with 4, 3).
Both halves have only a right child: not mirror images.

hints: Write a helper that tests whether two trees are mirror images of each other.
The left child of the first must match the right child of the second, and the other way round.
The tree is symmetric when its left and right subtrees are mirror images.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))

t = int(input())
vals = input().split()

print("yes" if symmetric(build_tree(vals)) else "no")

explanation: The two halves of the root are compared with a helper that crosses the children: left of one against right of the other.
